title: BCG vaccination against tuberculosis, in a district at low latitude
about: Thirteen real trials of the BCG vaccine (Colditz et al. 1994), read for a district that is invented. The trials and their counts are the published ones; the district, its baseline risk, the costs, the worth of a case averted, the discount rate and the study that could be run are this example's assumptions, stated so that they can be changed. The grading scheme is written after GRADE as an example and is not GRADE's own text. None of this is advice on vaccination.
theory:
theory bcg_vaccination
levels very_low low moderate high
node programme intervention: The district offers BCG vaccination to every newborn
node vaccinated output: Children are vaccinated in their first weeks with a potent vaccine
node cases outcome: Fewer children fall ill with tuberculosis
node burden impact: Less illness, death and cost from tuberculosis in the district
link programme -> vaccinated: clinics reach the births, and families accept the vaccine
support programme -> vaccinated: births are reached by the health service
support programme -> vaccinated: a cold chain to every clinic
link vaccinated -> cases: the vaccine protects those who receive it
support vaccinated -> cases: the vaccine's potency is kept until it is given
support vaccinated -> cases: children are vaccinated before they are infected
